card.statement:
Let $\varphi:C\to D$ be an étale map of curves.

(1)

We have $C^{(n)}_{[n]}\subset C^{(n)}_{\acute{\mathrm{e}}\mathrm{t}}$.

(2)

If $\varphi:C\to D$ is an open immersion, then $C^{(n)}_{\acute{\mathrm{e}}\mathrm{t}}=C^{(n)}$.

Since $C$ is a curve, any element $E\in C^{(n)}(S)$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor on $C\times S/S$, see [33, Tag 0B9D]. Its sheaf of ideals is the invertible sheaf

$\mathscr{O}_{C\times S}(-E)\subset\mathscr{O}_{C\times S},$

which satisfies

$\mathscr{O}_{C\times S}(-E)_{|(C\times S)\smallsetminus E}=\mathscr{O}_{(C\times S)\smallsetminus E}.$

2.4. $\mathbf{Y}_{\succeq 0}$ -graded symmetric powers of curves

We now recall a generalization of the constructions of §§2.2–2.3 that adds labels belonging to the positive coroot monoid $\mathbf{Y}_{\succeq 0}=\{\lambda\in\mathbf{Y}\mid\lambda\succeq 0\}$. If $\mu\in\mathbf{Y}_{\succeq 0}$, we will denote by $\mathfrak{P}(\mu)$ the set of partitions of $\mu$, i.e. unordered collections $[\lambda_{j}:j\in J]$ of elements of $\mathbf{Y}_{\succeq 0}\smallsetminus\{0\}$ such that $\sum_{j}\lambda_{j}=\mu$. (We allow here the empty collection, which provides the unique partition of $0$.)

From now on we fix $\mu\in\mathbf{Y}_{\succeq 0}$, and write $\mu=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathfrak{R}_{\mathrm{s}}^{\vee}}n_{\alpha}\cdot\alpha$. The associated partially symmetrized power of $C$ is

$C^{\mu}:=\prod_{\alpha\in\mathfrak{R}_{\mathrm{s}}^{\vee}}C^{(n_{\alpha})}.$

Then $C^{\mu}$ is a smooth scheme of dimension $\langle\mu,\rho\rangle=\sum_{\alpha}n_{\alpha}$. An $S$ -point of $C^{\mu}$ is a collection $E=(E_{\alpha}:\alpha\in\mathfrak{R}_{\mathrm{s}}^{\vee})$ such that, for each $\alpha\in\mathfrak{R}_{\mathrm{s}}$, $E_{\alpha}\in C^{(n_{\alpha})}(S)$. For brevity, in this setting we will write

$(C\times S)\smallsetminus E=(C\times S)\smallsetminus\bigcup_{\alpha\in\mathfrak{R}_{\mathrm{s}}^{\vee}}E_{\alpha}.$

We have a natural morphism

(2.7)

$C^{\mu}\to C^{(\langle\mu,\rho\rangle)}$

which sends a collection $(E_{\alpha}:\alpha\in\mathfrak{R}_{\mathrm{s}}^{\vee})$ to the effective Cartier divisor $\sum_{\alpha}E_{\alpha}$.

Let $\bar{k}$ be an algebraically closed field containing our base field $\mathbb{F}$, and let $E=(E_{\alpha}:\alpha\in\mathfrak{R}_{s}^{\vee})$ be a point in $C^{\mu}(\bar{k})$. Given a closed point $x$ in $C_{\bar{k}}$, we set

$\lambda^{E}_{x}=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathfrak{R}_{\mathrm{s}}^{\vee}}\dim_{\bar{k}}\Gamma(x,\mathcal{O}_{E_{\alpha}})\cdot\alpha\in\mathbf{Y}_{\succeq 0}.$

Let $x_{1},\ldots,x_{k}$ be the finitely many points such that $\lambda^{E}_{x}\neq 0$, and let $\Gamma_{E}$ be the (unordered) collection of elements of $\mathbf{Y}_{\succeq 0}$ given by

$\Gamma_{E}=[\lambda^{E}_{x_{1}},\ldots,\lambda^{E}_{x_{k}}].$

Then $\Gamma_{E}$ is a partition of $\mu$; we call it the Jordan type of $E$.

Given a partition $\Gamma\in\mathfrak{P}(\mu)$, we define a functor $C^{\mu}_{\Gamma}$ by

$C^{\mu}_{\Gamma}(S)=\left\{E\in C^{\mu}(S)\,\Big|\,\begin{array}[]{c}\text{for every geometric point $\bar{s}\to S$,}\\
\text{the point $E_{\bar{s}}\in C^{\mu}(\bar{s})$ has Jordan type $\Gamma$}\end{array}\right\}.$

This is a locally closed subscheme of $C^{\mu}$, and as in (2.4) we have a stratification

(2.8)

$C^{\mu}=\bigsqcup_{\Gamma\in\mathfrak{P}(\mu)}C^{\mu}_{\Gamma}.$

Here also, smoothness of strata follows from the following statement, which is a generalization of Lemma 2.1 taken from [12, §6.1].
card.label: Lemma 2.3

paper.title: Modular intersection cohomology of Drinfeld's compactifications
paper.abstract: We compute the dimension of the cohomology of stalks of intersection cohomology complexes on Zastava schemes and Drinfeld compactifications associated with a connected reductive algebraic group $G$, in case the characteristic of the coefficients field $\Bbbk$ is good for $G$. In particular, we show that these dimensions do not depend on the choice of $\Bbbk$.
